text:
I genuinely cannot praise Yell highly enough. They have built me a fantastic website, and the whole experience has been so much better than I ever expected.

My account manager, Russell, has gone above and beyond for me. He is absolutely brilliant — patient, kind, knowledgeable and always willing to help. Nothing ever feels like too much trouble, and he has taken the time to make sure I understand everything rather than making me feel silly for not being particularly technically minded!

The website-building team have been equally wonderful. They have really listened to what I wanted, taken my ideas on board and patiently made changes until the website looked and felt right for my business. As a self-confessed bit of a Luddite, I really appreciate how easy and enjoyable they have made the whole process.

Even the accounts team are brilliant. In fact, I am beginning to suspect that everyone who joins Yell is required to undergo some sort of rigorous kindness training! Every single person I have dealt with has been genuinely friendly, patient and helpful — but never in that false or sycophantic way. They are simply really nice people who are very good at their jobs.

I now have a website I am incredibly proud of, and I feel as though the people at Yell actually care about my business and want it to succeed.

A huge thank you to Russell and everyone involved. An absolutely first-class service from start to finish. Five very well-deserved stars.

text:
I had an extremely disappointing experience with Yell’s website service, and I regret choosing them.

Before signing the contract, I was told the website setup would take about a week before development started. Instead, the entire process dragged on for over a month and became incredibly stressful. I provided every page and all of the content they needed, but the website they produced looked very basic and unprofessional. It honestly felt like it had been built by someone with very little web design experience.

Rather than working with experienced web designers and developers, I found myself teaching their team how to build my own website. I spent four consecutive days explaining how the website should be designed, and even then it was still incomplete.

The booking form was one of the most important parts of my business. I even gave them a working example of how I wanted it built, but they failed to implement it correctly. I also tested the booking system they created, and it leaves customers stuck halfway through the process without taking them anywhere. In my opinion, this is a serious issue that could easily cost businesses potential customers. It seemed they either lacked the technical knowledge or the professional experience needed to build the functionality correctly.

Even their own website checking tools identified numerous issues that required improvement, yet these problems remained unresolved.

During the sales process, I was left with the impression that I was hiring a professional British company that would take care of everything for me. Unfortunately, the reality was very different. Once the contract was signed, I had to chase them constantly for updates and corrections. I called them three times within the first month asking to cancel the contract because I had already lost confidence in their ability to deliver, but my requests were refused.

At the moment, my app shows 21 leads. However, 15 of those were simply test submissions made by Yell themselves while testing my website. Of the remaining six, none resulted in a confirmed booking, and two weren’t even related to my services. From my perspective, this has been a complete loss of time and money.

Another major issue is the tracking phone number they provide. I cannot directly call customers back using that number, so I’m forced to contact them from my personal mobile instead. Many customers don’t answer unknown mobile numbers, which I believe has caused me to lose potential jobs and genuine leads.

I paid around £800 for a website that I don’t believe will help my business. I even accepted that financial loss and asked them to cancel my contract, but because it is a business-to-business agreement, I was told I would still have to continue paying regardless of whether the leads generated turned into actual work.

In my opinion, Yell needs to invest in experienced web developers, professional web designers, and better software if they want to compete in today’s market and deliver the quality of service customers are promised.

This entire experience has caused me an enormous amount of stress and has had a serious impact on my mental wellbeing. What was promised during the sales process was not what I experienced as a customer.

Based on my personal experience, I cannot recommend Yell’s website design service. I strongly advise anyone considering their website package to fully understand what they are agreeing to before signing a contract.

I joined Yell on 8 July expecting professional marketing support for my business, viaUNO Cars.

Before signing up, I clearly explained to the salesperson, Devan Appalsamy, that I already had a professionally built website and did not want or need another one. Despite this, I later discovered I had been enrolled on a website package.

Since joining, I have made multiple attempts to contact Yell—roughly every couple of days—requesting to speak with Devan Appalsamy and later my account manager, Niall Reynolds, to resolve the issue and discuss leaving the contract. Hi Sandeep 

Thank you for sharing your detailed feedback. We sincerely appreciate you taking the time to outline your experience and concerns regarding our services. 

We are  continuously evaluating our overall proposition to ensure its relevance in the evolving digital landscape, particularly concerning AI-driven search. We are committed to addressing these areas to better serve our customers.

If you would like to reach out to us on contactus@yell.com our team will be happy to discuss your concerns in more detail.

Regards
Priya
text:
Anyone considering Yell’s services should insist on receiving a complete, itemised description of everything included in the proposed package before signing up. I found the package descriptions vague, which made it difficult to understand precisely what was being purchased and what limitations applied.

I would also strongly recommend obtaining written confirmation of anything explained verbally during the sales process. In my case, I specifically asked whether the website included in the package would use a simple template or could be designed more bespoke to our requirements. I was told that either approach was possible, provided the website did not exceed five pages. After signing the agreement, however, one of the first things I was told was that a bespoke design was not possible.

Experiences like this suggest there are inconsistencies between what is communicated during the sales process and what the delivery teams are actually able or authorised to provide. This needs to be addressed. To be fair, the teams have responded quickly and generally appear responsive, but good communication after purchase does not resolve a lack of clarity before the contract is agreed.

For B2B companies in particular, I would carefully question whether Yell represents the right investment. Yell now appears to operate partly as a digital marketing agency, but its original proposition as a searchable business directory is increasingly difficult to justify. In Google search results, a Yell listing is effectively a directory entry appearing within another search directory. With businesses and consumers increasingly using AI platforms to identify and recommend suppliers, I also saw no clear evidence that Yell has meaningfully integrated AI-driven vendor discovery into its offering.

Based on my experience so far, I cannot currently recommend the service. The packages need to be more clearly itemised, verbal commitments must match what is ultimately delivered, and the overall proposition needs to demonstrate greater relevance in an increasingly AI-led search environment.
title: Sales process lacks consistency, packages need clear itemization and the value for B2B businesses is Questionable

text:
I submitted a full listing, was told approval takes 2 days, and heard nothing for 4. I contacted customer service to chase the approval and, at the same time, clearly stated I did not want my phone number published. Nobody told me this was a problem. They said the request had been escalated to get the listing approved.

A day later I got a call that turned out to be a long, mandatory SEO sales pitch, I was asked about pricing, margins, travel radius, website traffic, and more, all framed as necessary to "list my business," while being used to push their paid services. I told the agent repeatedly, multiple times, that I did not want my number listed. He said "OK" each time. At the end of the call, he told me the listing was published. I checked the listing and found my number published, against explicit instructions I'd now given to two separate people. I went to live chat to get it removed. Instead of addressing what I'd actually said, I was met with a wall of scripted "guidelines" language, repeated regardless of what I typed. When I explicitly stated I was revoking my consent under GDPR, they didn't engage with that at all, just more guidelines, as if their internal policy overrides UK data protection law.

This isn't a case of me not understanding how the platform works. I gave clear, repeated, explicit instructions to two different people before anything was published, and was actively reassured both times. Yell published my personal data anyway, then treated a formal GDPR consent withdrawal as something to be managed with a script rather than a legal right. Followed all this up with an unsolicited email telling me what's "wrong" with my SEO.

I've now spent hours dealing with a problem they created, on top of a sales process that used data-gathering as leverage before I'd even agreed to anything.

If you're a business with any reason to keep your number off a public listing, be aware that "no" does not seem to register with their staff until it's already too late.

⭐☆☆☆☆ 1 Star

As the owner of OSLID LTD, this has become the worst professional decision I have ever made.

I pay £298 per month to Yell, and, after six months, I have not received a single reliable lead, genuine commercial contract or domestic customer that justifies this investment.

I signed up because I was told my website would be placed on the first page of Google and that, provided I had the capacity, I could expect between one and five potential contracts per month.

I knew £298 per month was a huge financial commitment for me, but I was given confidence that the service would quickly generate enough business to pay for itself.

Six months later, none of that has happened.

Today, if I search for "Commercial Cleaner in London", my website is still nowhere to be found after numerous pages of Google results.

I was also required to replace my own website with a Yell-built website and replace my own business telephone number with Yell's advanced call-tracking number, despite repeatedly explaining that I wanted to keep my original number visible.

The website itself lacked important keywords, and, when I raised this concern, I was effectively told that I could add them myself.

Another major concern was that my website went offline for a week, and I was the person who had to alert Yell about it. I then requested an explanation regarding their website monitoring systems and why nobody informed me that my website was down. I never received a satisfactory answer.

The quality of the contacts generated has also been extremely disappointing. The overwhelming majority were consultants and sales companies trying to sell me additional services rather than genuine customers. Some initially presented themselves in a way that made them appear connected to tender opportunities until I challenged them and discovered they were consultants.

The most disappointing aspect, however, has been how my concerns were handled.

After complaining about the lack of results, instead of resolving my concerns, I felt persuaded into signing another agreement by a sales manager called Sam, despite already being unhappy with the existing service. Within hours, I communicated that I no longer wanted to proceed, but my request was not actioned.

I have also been transparent about my financial hardship. I earn less than £2,000 per month, pay high rent, support my children and cover all my essential living expenses. This situation has now reached the point where I am borrowing money from family and friends to maintain payments for a service that has produced no measurable return.

The anxiety this is causing is enormous because I genuinely do not want to close OSLID LTD.

My advice to Yell is simple: be realistic during the sales process, focus on generating genuine customers instead of sales calls from consultants, proactively monitor the websites you manage, and show flexibility when a struggling small business explains that the service is not working.

At the very least, after six months of poor results, a significant reduction in the monthly fee should have been considered if the objective was to retain me as a customer.

I am not asking for special treatment. I am asking for fairness, transparency and common sense.

text:
My experience with Yell has been extremely disappointing and, unfortunately, what began in January 2026 remains an ongoing saga.

Immediately following a formal review of my campaign, I raised serious concerns regarding lead quality, lead classification, campaign performance and the overall value being delivered. I was informed that my Account Manager carried out an audit with his manager, both agreed there were concerns, and the matter was escalated internally. Despite this, the issues were ultimately rejected and I have yet to receive what I consider to be satisfactory evidence addressing the points raised.

A major concern was the classification of leads. I challenged whether supplier calls, missed calls, existing customers and other non-sales contacts should have been counted towards campaign performance and lead guarantee figures. Despite repeatedly requesting evidence, I do not believe these concerns have been properly addressed.

The performance of the campaign was also deeply concerning. Based on the figures provided to me by Yell, my analysis showed that the effective cost per conversion was in excess of £1,500. For any small business, that level of performance raises serious questions about campaign management, optimisation and value for money.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that since leaving Yell, my business has achieved dramatically different results. Under independent Google Ads management, I have generated more genuine enquiries and secured more new customers in approximately three months than I achieved during the eighteen months Yell managed the account. My current campaign is producing conversions at approximately £48 each and the business is now thriving.

I was also disappointed by the lack of transparency surrounding fees and advertising spend. Google publishes policies for third-party partners that emphasise transparency regarding services, fees and the management of advertising accounts. As a business owner investing significant sums each month, I believe clients should have clear visibility of where their money is being spent and exactly what value is being delivered.

Rather than reaching a satisfactory resolution, this dispute has continued since January and remains unresolved. Throughout the process I have repeatedly requested evidence to support the conclusions being presented, but I have found the responses largely consist of assertions rather than the underlying information required to independently verify the position.

Every business will have its own experience, but mine has been one of ongoing dispute, poor transparency, unresolved concerns and disappointing results relative to the investment made.

There is no lead guarantee, it should be called something else as it appeared to focus almost entirely on the quantity of enquiries rather than the quality of those enquiries.

As a business owner, I don't measure success by how many people contact me. I measure success by how many genuine opportunities are created and how many customers are won.

The impression I was left with was that once a contact had been recorded, the emphasis was on counting it towards the lead target rather than examining whether it represented a realistic sales opportunity for my business.

From my perspective, there seemed to be a significant difference between what Yell considered a lead and what I considered a genuine prospective customer.

That distinction matters because businesses do not grow from lead numbers on a report. They grow from relevant enquiries, quotations, sales and profitable work.

If a supplier call, a missed call, an existing customer, your Auntie or someone looking for a product you do not offer can all contribute towards a lead target, then business owners should look very carefully at how success is being measured before placing too much reliance on a lead guarantee.


If you are considering Yell, I would strongly recommend asking detailed questions about lead validation, campaign management, reporting transparency and exactly how your advertising budget is being allocated before signing any agreement.
Also go over their terms and conditions with a fine tooth comb before signing.

text:
I signed up with Yell after being given the impression during the sales process that the service would generate a steady flow of genuine enquiries and provide a worthwhile return on investment. The sales presentation was persuasive and created high expectations about the potential results.

Unfortunately, my experience after signing up was very different. Despite paying substantial monthly fees, the volume of genuine leads generated was extremely low and nowhere near what I had been led to expect. The few enquiries received did not come close to justifying the ongoing cost of the service.

What I found particularly frustrating was that when concerns were raised about the lack of results, the suggested solution often appeared to be increasing the advertising spend or upgrading to additional services in the hope of improving performance. In my case, I saw no evidence that spending more money would have delivered a better outcome.

I would also strongly encourage prospective customers to read the contract terms carefully before signing. My impression from the sales discussions was very different from the limitations and disclaimers contained within the agreement. While the sales pitch focused heavily on the results that could be achieved, the contractual terms made it clear that no particular level of enquiries or business could be guaranteed.

Another point prospective customers should be aware of is that business-to-business contracts do not generally provide the same cooling-off rights that consumers may be familiar with. Once committed, I found myself tied into an expensive agreement despite being disappointed with the results delivered.

Advertising always carries risk and no company can guarantee success. However, I felt there was a significant gap between the expectations created during the sales process and the reality of the service delivered. Based on my experience, the return on investment was poor and alternative marketing channels provided considerably better value.

My advice to other small business owners would be to read the contract carefully, understand the cancellation terms before signing, and make sure any expectations discussed during the sales process are reflected in writing. 

Prospective customers should also pay close attention to the website terms. I was surprised to discover that the website provided as part of the package was tied to the ongoing contract and would cease to be available if the agreement ended. Small businesses should make sure they fully understand what they will and will not retain at the end of the contract before signing.

UPDATE (24th June 2026)

As part of the package, Yell provided and managed my website, supplied a dedicated landline number which diverted calls to my mobile, and provided website contact forms through the website they controlled.

This led me to consider how enquiries are attributed and reported. For example, if an existing client refers someone to your business, that person then visits your website to check you out and subsequently contacts you using the published telephone number or contact form, how is that enquiry classified and reported?

I believe prospective customers should understand how website ownership, tracking telephone numbers and website contact forms interact with performance reporting, and should ask detailed questions about the methodology used.

With the benefit of hindsight, I would encourage prospective customers to ask detailed questions about website ownership, call-tracking numbers, lead attribution methodology, and whether the product is a good fit for their industry.

text:
I had been a customer of for around 18 months and always paid on time. I then entered into a new agreement for the Accelerate Tier 5 package with SEO bolt-on at a cost of approximately £2,549 per month plus VAT.

The package was sold heavily around Yell’s “Guaranteed Leads” proposition, which is advertised prominently across their website and sales material as “The UK’s only digital marketing agency that guarantees leads” The package breakdown presented to me was approximately:
• £1,600 Google Ads
• £800 Sponsored Listings
• £450 SEO

Based on those representations, my understanding was that the Google Ads(later discovered via GOTU, white label marketing- not proper Google campaign management as sold) allocation represented substantial actual advertising spend into Google campaigns, while the Sponsored Listings element related to advertising on Yell’s own platform.

However, over time I became increasingly concerned about the transparency of the package, the operation of the Lead Guarantee, and the actual allocation of advertising spend.

The biggest issue for me is that the reality of how the package appears to operate is very different from the impression created during the sales process and marketing. The Yell Web site has it big and bold "The UK’s only digital marketing agency that guarantees leads" Then the live chat pops up and big and bold "Guaranteed Leads, Exclusive to Yell"

For example:
• I later discovered that “margin fees” were embedded within the Google Ads allocation itself
• These management/margin fees were never separately itemised or visibly disclosed to me during the sales process
• The actual media spend versus retained management fees was never transparently reported but is understood to be around 50%. So £1600 Google Ad spend is actually £800 Google Ad spend and £800 for Yell Google Ad management.(This fee is important when we get to the performance)
• The Lead Guarantee itself appears subject to extensive conditions and internal reporting controls that are not obvious from the headline marketing claims.
In simple terms, the “Lead Guarantee” appears to mean:
Yell decide how leads are counted
Yell control the reporting
You still have to pay even if the guarantee is missed
Any credit is usually applied later, not automatically refunded
The guarantee is based on their calculations and definitions, not necessarily what a customer would view as a genuine lead
So while it is technically a “guarantee,” it operates more like:
a conditional account credit system controlled by Yell’s own terms and reporting.

I also formally raised concerns during the live agreement regarding lead delivery, reporting discrepancies, and lead quality. Despite this, no credit was ever disclosed or applied to my account at the time. It was only much later, during collections activity, (5 months later) that Yell alleged a credit had internally been calculated.

Another major concern was campaign performance itself. Yell’s own figures later disclosed over 22,000 clicks resulting in only 8 conversions (click to call, click to email or a form fill), with conversion costs exceeding £1,500 each over a 4 month reporting period. By comparison, my independently managed campaigns are currently achieving significantly stronger results at a fraction of the cost at 26 conversions at £48 per conversion during a 1 month reporting period. (These 26 conversions cost less than one conversion from Yell) The same 26 conversions would cost me £39,000 with Yell where as it costs £1248 with my new managed campaign. This leads to the 50% Google Ad management fee of £800. Are Yell qualified? Results would suggest, "Unlikely"

There were also periods at the start of the agreement where parts of the advertising setup reportedly could not connect properly to Facebook/social campaigns, yet full billing continued and no reconciliation or adjustment of advertising allocation was ever provided.

My concern is that the practical operation of this package, the Lead Guarantee, and the transparency around spend allocation were materially different from the impression created by the sales process and marketing.

Consider the following actions:
• Get a a full written breakdown of actual media spend versus management fees
• Ask exactly how leads are classified and counted (missed calls, supplier calls, same number calling you)
• Ask what happens operationally if the Lead Guarantee is missed. Ask for written clarification on the process via email.
• Request direct platform reporting from Google Ads itself to see your spend v margin/management fees
• Read the full terms and conditions very carefully before signing

This package is far more complex and conditional than the headline “Guaranteed Leads” marketing suggests
title: Beware of the so called "Guaranteed Leads" & “Stop paying for marketing that underperforms” Taglines

We recently had our business website built by Yell. The site went live as planned, but the design feels quite generic and not particularly tailored to our business.

text:

This means potential customers have no way of seeing the serious problems we experienced or the financial loss we suffered. Losing £40,000 to a builder who did not deliver what was promised has been incredibly distressing, and the whole point of leaving a review was to prevent others from going through the same situation.
If negative experiences are repeatedly removed when reported by the business involved, then the reviews on this platform cannot be considered balanced or reliable. Review sites should allow honest feedback, both positive and negative, so people can make informed decisions. At the moment, it feels like the system protects businesses rather than consumers.

text:
Dear Customer Services,



I am writing to raise a formal complaint regarding the advertising agreement I entered into with Yell in November, at a cost of £298.80 per month.



From the outset, the service has failed to deliver what was represented during the sales process. Since the agreement began, I have received no business leads whatsoever that can be attributed to Yell, which represents a complete lack of return on what is a significant monthly cost to my business.



Furthermore, at the beginning of the agreement I was promised an induction call/meeting in which I would be guided through the service and advised on how best to optimise the advertising and maximise enquiries. This induction never took place, meaning I was never given any professional guidance regarding the setup, content, or input required from my side in order for the advertising to perform effectively.



This failure at the very start of the agreement raises serious concerns about whether the service has ever been properly implemented.



My experience with customer support has also been extremely disappointing. During a phone call today with a member of your team, Rash, I explained that I wished to terminate the agreement due to the total absence of results. Rather than attempting to address the issue or escalate the complaint, I was simply told that the contract was for one year and could not be cancelled, after which the call was abruptly ended.



This level of service and handling of a customer complaint is not acceptable.



In addition, I must highlight that the service being delivered appears materially different from the service that was represented to me during the sales process. The agreement was entered into on the understanding that Yell’s advertising platform would actively generate customer enquiries for my business and that I would receive onboarding support to help optimise the listing. Given that no leads have been generated and the promised induction support was never provided, I am concerned that there has been a significant failure between the sales representation and the service actually delivered. I therefore request that this be reviewed as part of your formal complaints and compliance process.



Given:



The complete absence of leads or measurable return,
The failure to deliver the promised induction and onboarding support, and
The unsatisfactory response from your team when raising these issues,




I am formally requesting that this agreement be terminated without further financial obligation.



I must also state that, based on the difference between what was represented during the sales process and what has actually been delivered, I am concerned that the agreement may have been mis-sold. I would therefore ask that this matter be reviewed by your compliance or senior complaints team as part of this formal complaint.



If this matter cannot be resolved promptly, I will consider escalating the issue further, including submitting a complaint to the Advertising Standards Authority regarding the representations made during the sales process, and raising the matter with Trading Standards in relation to the service that has been delivered.



Please treat this message as a formal complaint and request for contract review. I would appreciate a written response within 7 days from a senior member of your customer services or account management team confirming how this matter will be resolved.



If I do not receive a satisfactory response within this timeframe, I will have little option but to review and formally dispute any further payments associated with this agreement while the complaint is under investigation.



Regards

Lee Davies

Countrywide Shutters

text:
Avoid this company at all costs.
My experience with Yell has been financially damaging, emotionally draining, and riddled with systemic failures across almost every department I dealt with.

Apologies to Conor the account manager for having to write this.  He was a very nice and helpful guy.  The failings are systematic and nothing to do with him. 

I signed up for what was sold to me as a performance-based acquisition system designed to bring in paying customers. That was repeated across multiple calls and never corrected. In reality, what I received was a stream of low-quality, irrelevant enquiries that did not match the service I provide. This was completely different from the product that was advertised and sold to me.

Over six months, I paid approximately £6,000 for a service that failed on every level:

▪ Zero proactive campaign management

Ads were left switched off for long periods without anyone noticing.
When I asked why basic marketing fundamentals were missing (retargeting, exclusions, lookalikes, job-title targeting), I was told ads are “not proactively managed unless clients complain.” That alone speaks volumes.

▪ Wrong targeting and wrong messaging

Despite providing detailed instructions again and again, Yell repeatedly advertised the wrong message, the wrong offer, and targeted the wrong regions and demographics.

▪ Severe billing issues

Yell took duplicate payments, charged more months than agreed, and then told me to sort it out through my bank - something no reputable company should ever tell a customer. Months later, key refunds still were not resolved.

▪ Complete breakdown in communication

I raised multiple formal complaints.
Not one was acknowledged or responded to within the timeframes they themselves set.
Even now, they have not provided the required resolutions.

▪ Massive impact on my business

Before using Yell, my coaching business was stable with strong client numbers.
After months of failed delivery, wasted ad spend, mismanagement, and time spent correcting their errors, my business fell into serious financial distress.

I was forced to run my own ads at £5/day just to stay visible, because I had no budget left - all my capital was tied up in a system that did not function.

▪ Hours of my own time wasted

I spent countless hours writing emails, rewriting ad copy, guiding their staff, reviewing errors, submitting complaints, and trying to help them deliver the product I had already paid for. None of this work should ever fall on the client.

The only positive

Conor, the account manager, was polite and made genuine efforts - but even he was blocked by Yell’s broken internal systems. The problem is not staff like him. The problem is the structure, the lack of capability, and the systemic failures in the organisation.

Bottom line:

Yell sold me one thing, delivered something completely different, mishandled my payments, ignored my complaints, damaged my business, and wasted months of my time.

I cannot recommend strongly enough that businesses avoid Yell.

There are far better marketing services out there, and many far cheaper ones that will still outperform what I received.

As Yell have not responded or acknowledged my official complaint emails I have had to raise with the ASA, Trading Standards, ICO, CMA and prepare for small claims court.  I appreciate the polite response Penny however I’ve tried to settle this amicably for months now.

Yell's website design was subpar even after multiple revisions, and the traffic I received was mostly spam calls and texts. Attempting to cancel my £360/month subscription proved futile, as I'm locked into a 12-month contract and faced threats of debt collectors. I urge potential Yell Business customers to explore alternatives like Google, Instagram, or Facebook ads. 

My client manager at Yell has been exceptionally supportive, and everyone I've interacted with has been understanding and helpful given my current circumstances. I have no complaints about any individual on the team. However, my main concern lies with the overall business practices. Entering into a 12-month contract without guaranteeing the expected results for the majority of customers feels unethical.

I'm still seeking to cancel my subscription, but doubt Yell's willingness to prioritize customer satisfaction over profit.

*Updated Review as of 15/09/2025*
Quick update – someone from the Yell team got in touch regarding my issue with the monthly subscription, and they were actually able to switch my package over to Google Ads instead of just promoting on Yell. Once they did that, I started seeing more clicks and better interaction with my business.

To be honest, I think Yell’s business model is focused way too much on pushing you to advertise on their own platform, even though barely anyone actually uses Yell to search for services anymore — most people just Google it. So the fact they prioritise their own listings over running proper Google Ads for you is a bit frustrating.

That said, the person I spoke to was helpful, and after switching to the Google Ads option, I did get better results. I ended up staying on for another 3–4 months before cancelling, which I did straight away once the term ended.

If you’re considering Yell, I’d definitely recommend pushing for the Google Ads package, not just their own platform listings. The listings are technically free, but honestly, the leads you get are low quality and not worth much. Get them to advertise your business on Google — that’s the only way you’ll see real value.

I’ve changed my review from 1 star to 3 stars because they eventually sorted the issue, but I still feel the service overall wasn’t worth the money I was paying.

Every month, we help millions of consumers find the local services they need, while businesses across the UK benefit from our powerful digital marketing solutions to be found, trusted, and chosen online. We want to transform everyday business to improve everyday life.

Digital marketing solutions provider

As the UK’s number one for managed digital advertising for local businesses*, and 50+ years of experience, we know how to help your business grow.

Over the years, hundreds of thousands of businesses have trusted Yell’s marketing services. In fact, some of our clients have been with us for over 30 years!

We build and manage digital marketing solutions that help your business to get the leads you actually want. As a partner of Meta and Microsoft, as well as one of the UK’s top Google partners**, we know how to level up your marketing and drive your business’s success.

From your business profiles, reviews, social media, websites, and advertising campaigns across search engines and social media, we do it all as part of an all-in-one managed digital marketing solution.

We offer 3 powerful digital marketing solutions that will be tailored to your business, industry, ideal customers, and goals:

Activate

Activate is great for businesses who want to be found online, apply for customer jobs & build credibility.

Amplify

Amplify is ideal for businesses who want a strong online presence and a professional, conversion-focused website (trust us – we’ve built over 140,000!).

Accelerate

Accelerate is perfect businesses who want to reach ready-to-buy customers across multiple platforms and drive leads.

Features you get as part of our digital marketing solutions:

  • A strong online presence across up to 58 platforms
  • Ads across Yell.com & the Yell app to drive ready-to-buy enquiries
  • Instant access to local customer leads with Yell Ads & Jobs
  • Request & manage Yell reviews
  • Post across social media platforms in a tap
  • Easily manage reviews across platforms (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • A conversion-focused website (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • Expertly managed search, social & display ads (Accelerate exclusive)
  • Help & support just a call or message away
  • Advice & guidance to help get the most out of your solution
  • Manage your solution & view performance via the app
  • Updates to your profiles, website & ads whenever needed (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • Regular performance reviews & optimisations (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • Advanced call tracking & analytics (Accelerate exclusive)
  • A dedicated account manager (Accelerate exclusive)

Let us take care of your marketing so you can focus on what you do best – running your business.

Want to grow your business? Let's get started today. Call us on 0800 777 445 or visit our website.

text:
I was on Yell for a number of years paying over £800 a month for sponsored advertising. Firstly, lately the other well known platforms seem to be much better value for money, get you more leads and more solid work - a £50 per month post on Facebook would get you more leads than £800 on yell.. I know this to be true as I do it. Secondly, the customer service has all of a sudden turned terrible, taking weeks for a reply from your business rep about serious problems - you get frequent random calls from yell to offer you websites for thousands of pounds or to add areas to your listing etc but never there to talk to you about real issues. Just £££ is the only concern!! As well as this, they have taken payments earlier than agreed which obviously isn’t ideal. All in all Yell served me well for 4 years and didn’t have much to complain about, the past 2 years and judging by other trades opinions it is only going downhill. I am no longer staying with Yell after realising what you can get elsewhere for that kind of money. AVOID.. text:
Like others,  I had the great sales pitch and it all sounded great and I signed up for a year of website because my current website was badly in need of a refresh. The website builder seemed professional, but then website went live without me being told and without me checking it. My old website disappeared and the email account that went with it disappeared too. 2 days later after not getting any business emails and about a day of messing about with my email provider to find the cause, did i find out what had happened. I saw the new website and although it was good for a first attempt it was very basic compared to my current website and totally not ready for public to see. I was prepared to do work on it to get it good, but it was a total shock that it was already published and taking the place of my functioning busines website. I was very cross and managed to get it taken down and old website put up (which i realised was not so bad at all in comparison) and got my emails working again, However, i totally lost 2 days of emails. My provider said there was no way they could be retrieved!!! I work with lawyers and solicitors and clinical partners as well as potential customers, so that was very bad indeed. I cancelled everything that Yell was doing,and paid up for the whole year over £450 because i wanted to draw a line under thisbad experience and didn't want the hassle and stress with monthly payments and trying to remember to cancel or bailifs etc. Now i still have the free listing up. Today i had a yell messaging email to say i had received a new message. I went to the app on my ipad and read the message and phoned up the person and it turns out they had written that message 2 months ago and had already found another company to supply what they need. The date on the app of the message was 3.11.21 and today is 26.1.22. I did a test message to myself. The cute message bot said that my company will respond within 24 hours. That was at 4pm today. Well now it is 11pm and i have not had any email from Yell messaging to say there is a message waiting, but if i look on the app,my message is there. Basically if you want to use this service you will need to check the app everyday on not rely on an email being sent to you (even though i got the yell messaging email today for the november message). I am going to close down my free listing on  yell.com because people can find me easy enough via google and i don't want to have people leaving messages that i don't realise are there.
Update: today I phoned yell to discuss the problem with the free listing and not being notified of the message. Was told that there is no system currently for notifiying you via email of messages but they are looking into this for the future. I was able to turn off the messaging function, so that i don't need to constantly check the app for messages that might be sitting there. I spoke to 2 people on the phone and both were very helpful and friendly. I have decided to keep my free listing as it is still advertising and people can get to my website and phone number from there, so it is not all bad. I have changed my stars from 1 to 3 now as a result.

I also repair my shoes.

Every month, we help millions of consumers find the local services they need, while businesses across the UK benefit from our powerful digital marketing solutions to be found, trusted, and chosen online. We want to transform everyday business to improve everyday life.

Digital marketing solutions provider

As the UK’s number one for managed digital advertising for local businesses*, and 50+ years of experience, we know how to help your business grow.

Over the years, hundreds of thousands of businesses have trusted Yell’s marketing services. In fact, some of our clients have been with us for over 30 years!

We build and manage digital marketing solutions that help your business to get the leads you actually want. As a partner of Meta and Microsoft, as well as one of the UK’s top Google partners**, we know how to level up your marketing and drive your business’s success.

From your business profiles, reviews, social media, websites, and advertising campaigns across search engines and social media, we do it all as part of an all-in-one managed digital marketing solution.

We offer 3 powerful digital marketing solutions that will be tailored to your business, industry, ideal customers, and goals:

Activate

Activate is great for businesses who want to be found online, apply for customer jobs & build credibility.

Amplify

Amplify is ideal for businesses who want a strong online presence and a professional, conversion-focused website (trust us – we’ve built over 140,000!).

Accelerate

Accelerate is perfect businesses who want to reach ready-to-buy customers across multiple platforms and drive leads.

Features you get as part of our digital marketing solutions:

  • A strong online presence across up to 58 platforms
  • Ads across Yell.com & the Yell app to drive ready-to-buy enquiries
  • Instant access to local customer leads with Yell Ads & Jobs
  • Request & manage Yell reviews
  • Post across social media platforms in a tap
  • Easily manage reviews across platforms (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • A conversion-focused website (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • Expertly managed search, social & display ads (Accelerate exclusive)
  • Help & support just a call or message away
  • Advice & guidance to help get the most out of your solution
  • Manage your solution & view performance via the app
  • Updates to your profiles, website & ads whenever needed (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • Regular performance reviews & optimisations (Amplify & Accelerate only)
  • Advanced call tracking & analytics (Accelerate exclusive)
  • A dedicated account manager (Accelerate exclusive)

Let us take care of your marketing so you can focus on what you do best – running your business.

Want to grow your business? Let's get started today. Call us on 0800 777 445 or visit our website.

*We’re number 1 among direct competitors (those that target local businesses regardless of the customer’s industry)

text:
I own a driving school, which just before the pandemic struck altered status from sole trader to limited company. The driving school has advertised its business through yell.com in York, Scarborough and Malton for over 11 years. Over the 11 years a bond was formed, I’d say of trust and confidence in that we were doing the right thing advertising through yell.com. This to such a a degree that in 2020 we asked yell to build us a new, expensive website and to manage said website. 
During the various lockdowns that followed, we have not been allowed to trade, so had no income. We received no financial support from the government and in order to survive we needed to ask some companies such as car lease companies and telecommunication companies to understand that we were not trading so were finding paying all outgoings difficult. Many other businesses were in the same boat of course! The least sympathetic company of all that we approached for some understanding was yell.com. They gave us a very tough time!
Thankfully we were allowed to begin working again on 12th April and we’re inundated with work so regular income is back to normal. We had a debt to yell.com, as the result of the lockdowns and loss of business, not a considerable debt, but nevertheless there was a debt. We’d arranged and agreed that one of their account managers would call us this week, so we set aside time in the diary for this appointment/conversation to take place, as it was important to us to make yell.com aware we are back trading as before and we wished to clear the debt. The call was not so important to yell.com it appears as the account manager failed to call us as arranged, so we called him. Very keen to get matters resolved and back to normal ASAP.
During the call with the account manager we made it clear we are now again in a position to pay our monthly advertising costs in full and we attempted to reach agreement on a plan to clear all arrears caused by the pandemic lockdowns before Christmas. Our offer, which was affordable and reasonable was rejected and yell.com told us they’d shut down our website and all our advertising within 48 hours unless we agreed to their terms. Their terms were unacceptable, unfair and unaffordable. We asked to speak with a manager so we could state our case to someone in authority, hopefully getting some support. We were told we could speak with a manager, but only AFTER they’d shut down all our business.
Then they said not only would they shut down the website and all advertising, but they’d pass the debt onto a third party collection agency to pursue us!
Yell.com became our worst nightmare, intent on destroying us it appeared. Our 11 year relationship and our desire to clear the debt within four months meant nothing to them!
Before the pandemic we were flourishing, looking to bring in more instructors and expand. Everything was going well. No one foresaw the pandemic and the devastating affect it would have on businesses. Come November we’ll have cleared our debt to yell.com, and we’ll then resume our business plan to expand our business. A business yell.com was willing to destroy! 
We contacted the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) desperate for advice. The FSB were shocked and appalled at yell.com’s position. We received support from the FSB so were able to meet yell.com’s demands so our advertising and website has not been closed down. But we feel we were pushed into a corner by yell.com, put into an impossible situation and blackmailed.
Two stars not one has been left for yell.com because the advertising we have with them does bring in a lot of business and we did not have any problems at all until the lockdowns caused by the pandemic.
The FSB gave us some good advice. “Do not have all your eggs in one basket. You have discovered you cannot trust yell.com as you thought you could, so move some of your advertising to other companies”.
We’ll be following that excellent advice this week!
We also used to receive one on one support from yell.com because of the amount of advertising we placed with them and because of the amount of money we are paying them. This was really useful as we grow the company. They withdrew that support a few weeks back.
You live and learn!
Updated 26th July. Yell.com responded to the review on 12th July saying one of the customer care team would contact me within 72 hours. 
Never heard from yell, so their claim they reviewed the account is untrue. There has been no review of my account at all. Yell have not called me regarding this review either, so that’s false. I’ve written to yells CEO Claire Miles.
Update as at 7th August 2021 - I have never received any call despite promises, no email despite promises & no response to letter sent to CEO. Customer services at yell.com is non existent in my experience!

text:
Disappointed and underwhelmed. I am trying to be fair hear and not just give a one star rating (like so m any others do) when things haven’t gone as I would have liked them to. We all want the magic answer when it comes to generating genuine hot leads and customers and as we all know this does not exist. Three stars is where Yell sit and on reflection that’s about right. 

I've used several of the products offered by Yell and I do like the continuity of having one point of contact to manage multiple products and essentially the advertisement campaigns that are running at any one time. The business dashboard is really useful having access to all of your products and campaigns but in particular being able to view the analytics of individual campaign performance. That information and knowledge is key when it comes to testing what works and engages with your audience and what doesn’t. Great.

That for me is where the positivity ends though. I will try to be concise and to the point about the negatives I have experienced.

The front end sales and on boarding process is very slick and I was impressed with this. It installed confidence that my monthly contract spend would be justified. Unfortunately that hasn't been the case. Since on boarding with Yell they have been slow to respond to queries and problems (often several days despite phoning and emailing). My advertisements have been incorrect every single month since joining Yell (4 months in). 

Now these things do happen but there in lies my biggest issue with Yell - Not only are they are slow to respond, react and correct. YOU WILL NOT HAVE CONTROL OF YOUR OWN ADVERTISEMENTS! You have to wait to have google and social ads changed by one of the teams. This often takes days not minutes. This is a big problem particularly if it is critical information to your campaign such as price or offer. This has to be done by phone, whilst screen sharing with a customer service advisor to get the wording correct which again takes a while. I don’t understand why as customers we can’t simply control this through our own dashboard - It could be checked by Yell afterwards for publishing...

Yell also have some antiquated views on wording and punctuation of advertisements - For instance Yell insist on capitalisation of every single word within an advertisement. I felt it made us look like and feel like unprofessional and incompetent - when you have family, colleagues and existing customers pointing out that the advertisements they saw promoting your business looked amateurish as a result. This can’t help attract new business. I asked for this to be corrected/changed but was told this is best practise. I challenged this by saying John Lewis, M & S, Nike, Apple (And many others) etc don’t do it but was simply told it cannot be changed. Whether this is correct or not is almost irrelevant in comparison with my main point……

We as the paying customer are not able to make that change and that is a massive problem and has been the final nail in the coffin for making my decision final. As the business owner I take joint responsibility for the content created around our adverts but the points I’ve raised above are not my fault and are quite simply not good enough.

The latest problem I've experienced in this past couple of weeks - Most of the information on my dashboard has vanished which gives me limited access to as service I'm paying for. Once again I have contacted Yell but as yet I have had no response. Interestingly they always invoice on time! No surprise there, very on the ball where it counts! For me perhaps Yell could and should try to make the customer service and technical side of their business as slick as their sales and invoicing departments. 

I will not be renewing my contract with Yell which is disappointing for both parties because I was fully prepared to be considerably more per month to attract the right sort of customers for my business. In the land of the blind, the one eyed man is King…...
title: Disappointed and underwhelmed
